title: Course Schedule
description: There are `numCourses` courses numbered from 0. Each pair `[a,b]` means course `b` must be completed before course `a`. Return true if it is possible to complete every course.
hints: Represent prerequisites as directed edges and process zero in-degree vertices.
A cycle prevents a complete ordering; unique orderings require a single available choice at each step.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean canFinish(int n,int[][] p) { List<Integer>[] g=new List[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g[i]=new ArrayList<>();int[] d=new int[n];for(int[] e:p){g[e[1]].add(e[0]);d[e[0]]++;}ArrayDeque<Integer> q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);int seen=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();seen++;for(int v:g[u])if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}return seen==n;} }

title: Course Schedule II
description: Return an ordering of all courses that satisfies the prerequisite pairs `[course, prerequisite]`. If multiple valid orders exist, return the lexicographically smallest one. Return an empty array if no valid ordering exists.
hints: Represent prerequisites as directed edges and process zero in-degree vertices.
A cycle prevents a complete ordering; unique orderings require a single available choice at each step.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int[] findOrder(int n,int[][] p) { List<Integer>[] g=new List[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g[i]=new ArrayList<>();int[] d=new int[n];for(int[] e:p){g[e[1]].add(e[0]);d[e[0]]++;}PriorityQueue<Integer> q=new PriorityQueue<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);int[] out=new int[n];int k=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();out[k++]=u;for(int v:g[u])if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}return k==n?out:new int[0];} }

title: Verify Alien Word Ordering
description: The string `order` lists the characters of an alien alphabet from smallest to largest. Return true if `words` is sorted lexicographically according to that alphabet. A word that is a prefix of another must come first.
constraints: order is a permutation of lowercase English letters
hints: Represent prerequisites as directed edges and process zero in-degree vertices.
A cycle prevents a complete ordering; unique orderings require a single available choice at each step.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean isAlienSorted(String[] w,String o) { int[] r=new int[26];for(int i=0;i<26;i++)r[o.charAt(i)-'a']=i;for(int k=1;k<w.length;k++){String a=w[k-1],b=w[k];int i=0;while(i<a.length()&&i<b.length()&&a.charAt(i)==b.charAt(i))i++;if(i==b.length()&&a.length()>b.length())return false;if(i<a.length()&&i<b.length()&&r[a.charAt(i)-'a']>r[b.charAt(i)-'a'])return false;}return true;} }

title: Minimum Height Trees
description: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to `n - 1`, return all node labels that can be chosen as a root to produce a tree of minimum height. Return labels in increasing order.
constraints: The input forms a connected tree
hints: A tree’s height is minimized when rooted at one of its center nodes.
Repeatedly remove all current leaves until one or two nodes remain.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public List<Integer> findMinHeightTrees(int n,int[][] e) { if(n<=2){List<Integer>a=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)a.add(i);return a;}List<Set<Integer>>g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g.add(new HashSet<>());for(int[] x:e){g.get(x[0]).add(x[1]);g.get(x[1]).add(x[0]);}List<Integer> q=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(g.get(i).size()==1)q.add(i);int left=n;while(left>2){left-=q.size();List<Integer> z=new ArrayList<>();for(int u:q){int v=g.get(u).iterator().next();g.get(v).remove(u);g.get(u).clear();if(g.get(v).size()==1)z.add(v);}q=z;}Collections.sort(q);return q;} }

title: Sequence Reconstruction
description: Each sequence contains labels from 1 through `n`. Return true if `nums` is the only possible shortest common supersequence of all sequences, meaning the directed ordering constraints determine every adjacent pair in `nums` uniquely. Otherwise return false.
constraints: Each sequence value is in [1, nums.length]
hints: Represent prerequisites as directed edges and process zero in-degree vertices.
A cycle prevents a complete ordering; unique orderings require a single available choice at each step.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean sequenceReconstruction(int[] nums,int[][] seqs) { int n=nums.length;List<Set<Integer>>g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<=n;i++)g.add(new HashSet<>());int[] d=new int[n+1];boolean[] seen=new boolean[n+1];for(int[] s:seqs){for(int x:s)seen[x]=true;for(int i=1;i<s.length;i++)if(g.get(s[i-1]).add(s[i]))d[s[i]]++;}for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)if(!seen[i])return false;ArrayDeque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);int k=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){if(q.size()!=1)return false;int u=q.remove();if(k>=n||nums[k++]!=u)return false;for(int v:g.get(u))if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}return k==n;} }

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description: Return the length of the longest path of strictly increasing values in a matrix. From each cell you may move up, down, left, or right. You may not move diagonally or revisit a cell in a path.
hints: Model each ordering rule as a directed edge.
Use indegrees to process prerequisites and identify cycles or forced choices.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int longestIncreasingPath(int[][] a) { int m=a.length,n=a[0].length;int[][] d=new int[m][n];ArrayDeque<int[]>q=new ArrayDeque<>();int[][] dirs={{1,0},{-1,0},{0,1},{0,-1}};for(int i=0;i<m;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++){for(int[] z:dirs){int x=i+z[0],y=j+z[1];if(x>=0&&x<m&&y>=0&&y<n&&a[x][y]<a[i][j])d[i][j]++;}if(d[i][j]==0)q.add(new int[]{i,j});}int len=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){len++;for(int k=q.size();k>0;k--){int[] u=q.remove();for(int[] z:dirs){int x=u[0]+z[0],y=u[1]+z[1];if(x>=0&&x<m&&y>=0&&y<n&&a[x][y]>a[u[0]][u[1]]&&--d[x][y]==0)q.add(new int[]{x,y});}}}return len;} }

title: Parallel Courses
description: There are `n` courses labeled 1 through `n`. Each relation `[a,b]` means course `a` must be completed before course `b`. Any number of courses may be taken in one semester if all prerequisites are complete. Return the minimum number of semesters needed, or -1 if the requirements contain a cycle.
hints: Model each ordering rule as a directed edge.
Use indegrees to process prerequisites and identify cycles or forced choices.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int minimumSemesters(int n,int[][] r) { List<Integer>[]g=new List[n+1];for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)g[i]=new ArrayList<>();int[]d=new int[n+1];for(int[]e:r){g[e[0]].add(e[1]);d[e[1]]++;}ArrayDeque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);int sem=0,seen=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){sem++;for(int k=q.size();k>0;k--){int u=q.remove();seen++;for(int v:g[u])if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}}return seen==n?sem:-1;} }

title: Find Eventual Safe States
description: A node is safe if every possible path starting from it eventually reaches a terminal node (a node with no outgoing edges). Return all safe node labels in increasing order.
constraints: Each edge goes to a valid node; the graph may contain cycles
hints: Model each ordering rule as a directed edge.
Use indegrees to process prerequisites and identify cycles or forced choices.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public List<Integer> eventualSafeNodes(int[][] g) { int n=g.length;List<Integer>[]r=new List[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)r[i]=new ArrayList<>();int[]d=new int[n];for(int u=0;u<n;u++){d[u]=g[u].length;for(int v:g[u])r[v].add(u);}ArrayDeque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);boolean[]s=new boolean[n];while(!q.isEmpty()){int v=q.remove();s[v]=true;for(int u:r[v])if(--d[u]==0)q.add(u);}List<Integer>out=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(s[i])out.add(i);return out;} }

title: Alien Dictionary Order
description: A sorted list of words is written in an unknown alphabet. Infer one valid character order consistent with the list. Return the lexicographically smallest valid order of all distinct characters present, or an empty string if the ordering is invalid or cyclic. When comparing words, the first differing character determines their order; a longer word cannot precede its own prefix.
hints: Model each ordering rule as a directed edge.
Use indegrees to process prerequisites and identify cycles or forced choices.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public String alienOrder(String[] w) { boolean[] seen=new boolean[26];int count=0;for(String s:w)for(char c:s.toCharArray())if(!seen[c-'a']){seen[c-'a']=true;count++;}List<Set<Integer>>g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<26;i++)g.add(new HashSet<>());int[]d=new int[26];for(int k=1;k<w.length;k++){String a=w[k-1],b=w[k];int i=0;while(i<a.length()&&i<b.length()&&a.charAt(i)==b.charAt(i))i++;if(i==b.length()&&a.length()>b.length())return "";if(i<a.length()&&i<b.length()){int x=a.charAt(i)-'a',y=b.charAt(i)-'a';if(g.get(x).add(y))d[y]++;}}PriorityQueue<Integer>q=new PriorityQueue<>();for(int i=0;i<26;i++)if(seen[i]&&d[i]==0)q.add(i);StringBuilder out=new StringBuilder();while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();out.append((char)(u+'a'));for(int v:g.get(u))if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}return out.length()==count?out.toString():"";} }

title: Course Schedule IV
description: Each prerequisite pair `[a,b]` means course `a` must be completed before course `b`. For each query `[u,v]`, return true if `u` is a direct or indirect prerequisite of `v`, otherwise false.
hints: Model each ordering rule as a directed edge.
Use indegrees to process prerequisites and identify cycles or forced choices.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public List<Boolean> checkIfPrerequisite(int n,int[][] p,int[][] q) { boolean[][]r=new boolean[n][n];for(int[]e:p)r[e[0]][e[1]]=true;for(int k=0;k<n;k++)for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(r[i][k])for(int j=0;j<n;j++)r[i][j]|=r[k][j];List<Boolean>out=new ArrayList<>();for(int[]e:q)out.add(r[e[0]][e[1]]);return out;} }
